summary: Frontend-only regression + feature test for new CursorGlow ambient effect on Kedbyte marketing site. Verified rendering, layering (z-index), pointer-events, smooth spring lag, route stability across all 5 routes, click interactivity, and absence of framer-motion / React runtime errors.
action_items: (Optional, pre-existing - NOT introduced by CursorGlow) Framer-motion console warning: 'You are trying to animate maxWidth from "none" to "160". none is not an animatable value' — appears 6+ times. Some component is animating maxWidth from CSS default 'none' which Framer cannot tween. Investigate and initialize maxWidth with a numeric value (e.g. 0 or a px value) in the animate target component.

(Optional, pre-existing - NOT introduced by CursorGlow) Framer-motion console warning: 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative/fixed/absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' Likely from a useScroll target ref attached to a static-positioned element.
critical_code_review_comments: CursorGlow.jsx is clean: SSR-safe initialization (typeof window !== 'undefined'), proper event-listener cleanup, useSpring damping:50/stiffness:100 produces the requested lag, pointer-events:none on both layers prevents click blocking — all per spec.
Body background changed to transparent and html to #000 — correct so negative z-index fixed layers become visible.
Minor: useTransform is imported in CursorGlow.jsx but never used. Unused import — safe to remove.

Minor: The glow inner div has both inline `left/top` (set by smoothX/smoothY) AND `x: -50%, y: -50%`. This works (centers the 1400x1400 circle on cursor) but mixing positional translate transforms via inline style on a motion.div with spring-driven left/top means the spring drives layout (left/top) instead of transform — slightly less GPU-efficient than driving translateX/translateY. Consider switching to `transform: translate(calc(x - 50%), calc(y - 50%))` via x/y motion values for better performance on lower-end devices. Not a bug — purely a perf nit.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CursorGlow implementation verified: (a) DOM contains both layers — class 'fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none bg-black' at z-index -2, and the spring-animated glow at z-index -1. (b) html bgcolor = rgb(0,0,0); body bgcolor = rgba(0,0,0,0) (transparent) as required. (c) Cursor lag confirmed — when mouse was moved to (1800,1000) the spring-driven inner div was still at (1725.84, 957.47) inline, proving damped follow. (d) All 5 routes (/, /services, /about, /careers, /contact) render glow and the custom Cursor dot+ring simultaneously without breakage. (e) Header z-index = 50 → above glow at -1 → glow is correctly BEHIND content. Custom cursor at z-index 9999. (f) Clicking 'Services' nav link navigated successfully to /services — pointer-events:none on glow does not block. (g) Zero uncaught page errors; zero framer-motion errors directly from CursorGlow/useSpring. (h) Two pre-existing framer-motion warnings remain (maxWidth animate-from-none and scroll-offset static-position) but these existed before this iteration and are unrelated to CursorGlow.
rca of the issue: N/A — no defects found in the CursorGlow feature. Pre-existing framer-motion warnings are noted as low-priority cleanup items but do not affect functionality.
